title.narrative: CODE 1_2025_Access to renewable energy - Promoting energy-efficient cooking stoves and solar lighting

description.narrative: Every sunset brings a new set of challenges for 5 community people in Maforki, and Beke-Loko chiefdoms, Port Loko district. At the same time, due to the lack of grid power or electricity and the remoteness of these communities, energy for house lighting is sourced mainly from paraffin lamps, torch lights, candles or Chinese-made battery lights (these batteries are costly to replenish and do not serve long). This has a profound effect especially on the women and school-going children who have to do their house chores and school studies respectively by use of paraffin lamps. The paraffin lamps have a poor spectrum of light that affects the users’ eyesight, irritates eyes and emit smoke that leads to respiratory infections and add to the global greenhouse emissions. Increased population and need for development has led to encroachment into the reserve area corridors and a reduction of the land available, this has inevitably led to competition for land and other natural resources. This project will promote the use of solar lighting for 182 households across five pilot communities, using a market-based approach, working with women’s groups as catalysts across the target communities, to test the appetite for clean solar lighting and willingness of communities to pay for these over a reasonable period of time. This will reduce prevalence of energy poverty for women and men, boys and girls and their communities across the five pilot communities.
